summary: Flutter's local LiveKit SDK fork now uses the web client's six-attempt exponential reconnect schedule with the same 0.8–1.2 jitter multiplier. Flutter and macOS/Android builds pass; peer-driven native reconnect timing remains unverified.

checks.name: Web reconnect schedule reference
checks.observation: The web suite passed 9 tests. BoundedVoiceReconnectPolicy yields base delays [250, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000, 4000] multiplied by a uniformly sampled 0.8–1.2 jitter factor, then stops after six attempts.

checks.name: LiveKit SDK fork reconnect policy
checks.observation: Three focused tests passed for all six base delays, lower/upper jitter boundaries, and rejection outside the attempt budget. The engine schedules from this tested helper and uses its attempt limit.

checks.name: Flutter app regression and full suite
checks.command: cd desktop && flutter test && flutter analyze
checks.observation: All 224 Flutter app tests passed and flutter analyze reported no issues.

checks.name: Android debug and macOS release compilation
checks.command: cd desktop && flutter build apk --debug && flutter build macos --release
checks.observation: Both builds passed against the local livekit_client 2.13.0 path override. Flutter emitted the existing Kotlin Gradle Plugin migration warning for Android and Xcode 27 emitted its x86_64 guidance; neither blocked compilation.

checks.name: Native peer-driven reconnect runtime
checks.observation: No Android device is currently visible in adb, and no two-peer network interruption was performed on macOS/Android. The computed delays match source-level web policy, but wall-clock runtime acceptance remains pending.

remaining: With a second peer available, induce and restore network loss on macOS and Android and verify observed retry timing, participant/media restoration, exhaustion message, and lease release.
